mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days without regime dependence as lower rates increase present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.0% and rises by more than 0.5 percentage points over three months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and decline in unemployment rate signals a strong economy with tightening monetary policy, causing short-term equity sell-offs as growth expectations are priced in over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.5%), a sustained decline in unemployment signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5% and UNRATE declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1,100,000 units, it signals strong consumer confidence and construction activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days as the economy expands.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1100.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as market participants anticipate strong corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and INDPRO fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In low industrial production growth regimes (INDPRO growth rate < 1.0%), a subsequent acceleration in industrial output signals a manufacturing recovery, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days as the economy shifts from contraction to expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth rate < 1.0% and INDPRO accelerates, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
